title: Age and Basic Eligibility Criteria
content: Applicants must be between 21 and 60 years of age at the time of application. Supported employment types include Salaried, Self-Employed, and Business. Unsupported employment types like Freelance or Unemployed require adding a primary salaried co-applicant.

title: EMI Calculation and Reducing Balance Interest
content: EMIs are calculated using the standard reducing balance interest formula: EMI = P · r · (1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n − 1), where P is principal loan amount, r is monthly interest rate, and n is total tenure in months. Longer tenures reduce monthly EMI but increase total interest payable.

title: EMI-to-Income Ratio Thresholds
content: The EMI-to-Income ratio combines requested loan EMI and existing monthly EMIs divided by monthly gross income. An EMI ratio below 40% qualifies for instant approval (if credit score >700). An EMI ratio between 40% and 60% moves the application to Officer Review. EMI ratio exceeding 60% leads to automated rejection.

title: Credit Score Impact and Benchmarks
content: Credit score benchmark for instant approval is >700. Scores between 600 and 700 are considered moderate and placed under Officer Review. Scores below 600 indicate elevated credit risk. Applicants can improve credit scores over 3-6 months by clearing active credit card dues and maintaining 0 late payments.

title: Personal Loan Terms
content: Personal Loans carry a 12.0% annual interest rate with a minimum monthly income requirement of ₹25,000 and maximum tenure of 60 months (5 years).

title: Home Loan Terms
content: Home Loans feature an attractive 8.5% annual interest rate with a minimum monthly income requirement of ₹40,000 and maximum tenure of up to 360 months (30 years).

title: Auto Loan Terms
content: Auto Loans feature a 9.5% annual interest rate, minimum monthly income requirement of ₹30,000, and maximum tenure of 84 months (7 years).

title: Education and Business Loan Terms
content: Education Loans feature a 10.0% annual interest rate with ₹20,000 min income requirement. Business Loans feature a 14.0% annual interest rate with ₹50,000 min income requirement and max tenure of 60 months.

title: What Does Review Status Mean?
content: A Review status indicates your application meets minimum safety thresholds but requires manual assessment by a Senior Credit Officer. The officer evaluates overall debt capacity, stability of income, and potential term adjustments before issuing final approval.

title: How to Improve a Rejected Application
content: If your application is rejected due to high EMI ratio, you can lower your requested loan amount by 10%–30% or extend loan tenure. For hard eligibility rejects (age or income), adding a co-applicant or guarantor resolves eligibility constraints.

title: Required Documents for Verification
content: Required pre-screening documents include: 1. Aadhaar / PAN card for identity, 2. Salary slips / Income tax returns (ITR) for past 3 months, 3. Bank statement for past 6 months showing salary credit or business revenue.

title: Existing EMI Obligations and Debt Burden
content: Existing EMIs directly reduce available monthly borrowing capacity. Paying off existing small personal loans or credit card converted EMIs immediately improves your EMI ratio and unlocks higher loan approval eligibility.

title: Co-Applicant and Guarantor Benefits
content: Adding an eligible co-applicant (spouse, parent, or working child) combines monthly household income, significantly lowering the overall EMI ratio and enabling higher loan amounts.

title: Interactive What-If Term Calculations
content: Applicants and Officers can simulate custom loan amounts, tenure months, and product types using the live What-If calculator. Calculations strictly use reducing balance formulas to show exact EMI and ratio outcomes.

title: Officer Discretion and Final Authority
content: The pre-screening tool provides automated guidance and recommendations, but all final loan approvals, interest rate discounts, and disbursement approvals are made exclusively by authorized credit officers.
